description: Check cited links or quotations in supplied source text, without AI. Use this to check 1-10 cited public HTTPS links before relying on them, in one call. Send urls to check links, or citations to also check a quotation per link: each quote is matched against the same retrieval with Quote Checker's literal rules (case, punctuation, and word boundaries preserved; whitespace normalized) and returns up to three original passages with offsets and, for PDFs, page numbers. Returns, per link, the final URL, redirects, HTTP status, content type, title, content hash, and a specific failure reason. Readable means the reader got extractable text; it does not show the page is accurate or supports a claim. A quote match means the words appear, not that they support the claim. Failed means this reader could not read it, which can mean a dead link or a site that refuses automated requests, needs JavaScript or a login, or disallows BOZOSReader in robots.txt; its quotation is then unchecked (quote_check null). Uses the guarded Source Reader. Content is not retained. Repeat a URL for multiple quotations: each distinct requested URL is read once per batch (fragments ignored, query strings preserved, redirect aliases kept separate). Sources are retrieved again in later requests. Optional unique citation ids are echoed on success and failure. Results explain offsets, matching rules, checked text representation and lengths, and distinguish matches_truncated from source_truncated. Inspect individual results even when HTTP or MCP reports a successful batch. For text your agent already has, send sources [{id,source_text,source_truncated?}] and citations [{source_id,quote,id?}]. Several citations can share a source_id. These checks make no source-fetch requests and return status supplied_text, null URL/HTTP/retrieval metadata, and a checked_text_sha256; they do not verify origin or authenticity. Mixed URL and supplied-text batches are allowed. summary.supplied counts supplied-text entries separately from readable URLs. Set source_truncated true for excerpts or incomplete input so missing quotations remain inconclusive. All supplied text is checked literally, including markup. Use POST or MCP for text; encoded GET bodies are also supported. Entire requests, including JSON/MCP overhead, are limited to 64 KiB. Failed URL entries carry upstream metadata (including robots-versus-source stage and Retry-After seconds) and a recovery hint. Delays belong to individual entries; a mixed batch never sets a whole-response Retry-After or retries sources automatically. To read a page before choosing quotations, call readSource with include_quote_source:true, then supply its quote_source.source_text and source_truncated without refetching. Retain the original reader response for URL provenance; submitted text is still labeled supplied_text. Same as POST https://bozos.si/api/v1/citation-check.

inputSchema.description: Supply exactly one of urls or citations. Optional sources requires citations; source_id references must exist and supplied-text citations require quote. Source IDs and citation IDs must each be unique in their own list.

citations.description: 1–10 citations in result order. Use url with optional quote, or source_id with required quote. Repeated URLs share a retrieval; source_id references reuse the supplied text. Optional citation ids must be unique.

id.description: Optional non-blank citation identifier, unique within the batch; echoed unchanged on success and failure.

quote.description: The exact words attributed to this source.

source_id.description: References an id in sources. Use exactly one of url or source_id; source_id requires quote. No URL is fetched for this entry.

sources.description: Optional caller-supplied sources, only with citations. Refer to each by source_id. No URL provenance is accepted or verified. The entire request must fit within 64 KiB.

id.description: Non-blank source identifier, unique in sources.

source_text.description: Non-blank text checked literally, preserving original whitespace and offsets. Share it across citations instead of repeating the text. No markup removal, fetching, or code execution.

source_truncated.description: Set true for an excerpt or incomplete source. A missing quotation is then inconclusive for the complete source.

urls.description: Public HTTPS URLs to check, 1-10, in order, without quotations. Each uses the guarded Source Reader: robots.txt is respected, at most three redirects are followed, and scripts are not run.

name: checkCitations

error.description: Failure code, such as upstream_error, robots_disallowed, no_readable_content, unsupported_content_type, dns_failed, timeout, invalid_url, or private_destination. Null when readable.

http_status.description: Final HTTP status when the server answered. Null when no response was received or the check stopped before one.

id.description: Optional non-blank citation identifier, unique within the batch; echoed unchanged on success and failure.

quote.description: The quotation as supplied, when one was sent.

quote_check.description: Present when a quote was sent; null when the link could not be read.

matched.description: Null when the source was truncated and the quote was not found in the checked part.

page_end.description: PDF sources only: one-based page where the match ends.

page_start.description: PDF sources only: one-based page where the match starts.

matches_truncated.description: More passages matched than the three returned; this does not indicate an incomplete source.

full_characters.description: Code points in the full extraction or submitted text before any checker output limit; for incomplete supplied text the original document length is unknown.

source_truncated.description: Only part of the original source is represented: a fetched extraction exceeded the limit, or the caller declared supplied text incomplete. Missing quotations are inconclusive.

recovery.description: Suggested next step after a source failure. BOZOS does not retry or wait automatically. retry_later may succeed but is not guaranteed; honor upstream delay and client budgets. use_supplied_text refers only to text the caller is authorized to supply.

source_id.description: Supplied source identifier, present only for supplied-text results.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the response body after HTTP decompression.

status.description: readable: URL was fetched and text extracted; supplied_text: caller-provided text was checked without a fetch; failed: URL could not be read.

upstream.description: Present for failed source checks; null if no failing HTTP response was recorded. A robots response is not the page status.

retry_after_seconds.description: Parsed upstream Retry-After: nonnegative seconds or an HTTP-date converted to seconds at receipt, rounded up. Null for missing, malformed, or unrepresentable values; zero is a known elapsed/zero delay.

url.description: URL as supplied for URL citations; null for supplied-text citations.

summary.description: Counts citation entries, including repeats. total = readable + failed + supplied (treat omitted supplied as 0). Supplied text is not counted as a readable URL.

quotes.description: Present when citations were sent with quotes.

supplied.description: Present only when supplied-text citations were checked; counts these entries separately from fetched readable URLs.

title: Check cited links or quotations in supplied source text, without AI
